entries.title: Psalms 11:1
segments:
This psalm seems to have been written at a time when law and order were prostrate, and the wicked triumphed over the righteous. 
 
  Ye; addressed to David's timid and unbelieving friends, who counselled flight. 
 
  Flee as a bird; from

we have the counsel of those friends. 
 
Without firm confidence in God and a man will be liable to desert the post of duty, and expose himself to the rebukes of the Almighty, and to the triumphs of his foes.

entries.title: Psalms 11:3
segments: The foundations; of social order, truth, and piety.

entries.title: Psalms 11:4
segments:
His eyelids try; he sees the whole conduct of men, and will protect and save his friends and destroy his enemies.  The psalmist's reply to his unbelieving friends. 
 
However adverse may be the present state of the righteous, or prosperous that of the wicked, the end of the one will be joy and triumph, of the other defeat and ruin.
